html:
A Taiwanese film from 1989, directed by Hou Hsiao-hsien, about one family in the years after Japanese rule ended in 1945. It was the first film to show the 228 Incident of 1947, when the Nationalist government crushed an uprising and killed thousands of Taiwanese.

For four decades the massacre could not be discussed in public. The film came out two years after the end of martial law, and it touched the White Terror that followed the Nationalist retreat to the island. Tony Leung Chiu-wai plays a deaf photographer, a quiet witness to events he cannot speak about.

It won the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival, the first for a Chinese language film. It was a hit in Taiwan, and it helped open public debate about the island's past as Taiwan moved toward democracy.
